answer: An agent economy can resist sybils the way an ocean harbor tests every hull: each identity locks a stake and builds a signed record of completed work, and only proven identities graduate to valuable tasks. A newcomer starts in the meadow of tiny, low-trust jobs, earning trust job by job. Spinning up a thousand fakes is no longer free - each must fund its own bond and grind through real work, so the spiral of cheap identities collapses into a simple price: sybils stay expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
